title: Word 6 — On the Warfare between Flesh and Spirit in the Christian
attribution_note: Word 6 of 28 in the collection Short Moral-Instructive Words — see Word 1 for provenance.

pairs.en: Every Christian, as was said above, has two births: the old birth, which is of the flesh, and the new birth, which is of the Spirit; and these two are, in every respect, opposed to one another. The birth of the flesh is flesh; the birth of the Spirit is spirit. *“That which is born of the flesh is flesh, and that which is born of the Spirit is spirit”* [John 3:6]. And because these two births are opposed to one another, from this arises the enmity and warfare between flesh and spirit within the Christian: *“the flesh lusts against the Spirit, and the Spirit against the flesh.”*

sections.heading: The Flesh's Desires, Point by Point

pairs.en: The flesh wants to seek glory, honor, and riches in this world, but the spirit despises all these things and strives only for the eternal blessings, and so on. Thus *“the flesh lusts against the Spirit, and the Spirit against the flesh.”*

The Christian, as one renewed, must live not according to the flesh but according to the spirit, and must subject the flesh to the spirit, according to the apostolic exhortation: *“Walk in the Spirit, and you shall not fulfill the lust of the flesh”* [Galatians 5:16]. And this means to *“crucify the flesh with its passions and desires”* [Galatians 5:24], to *“make no provision for the flesh, to fulfill the lusts thereof”* [Romans 13:14], to *“abstain from fleshly lusts, which war against the soul”* [1 Peter 2:11], to *“walk in newness of life”* [Romans 6:4], not to let sin reign over us [Romans 6:12], but *“to live for Christ, who died for us and rose again”* [2 Corinthians 5:15].

sections.heading: The True Mark of a Christian

pairs.en: Beloved Christians! Let us examine ourselves: do we wage this inward warfare? Do we stand in this saving struggle? Do we walk in newness of life? Do we resist the inclinations and lusts of the flesh? Do we refuse to let sin reign and rule over us? For only those belong to Christ *“who have crucified the flesh with its passions and desires”* [Galatians 5:24]. What good is it to be called a Christian without being one? It is not the Christian name that reveals the true Christian, but the struggle against the flesh and against every sin. Not everything the flesh demands should be granted to it. It demands food, it demands drink, it demands clothing, it demands rest, and other things it needs — let us give these. But when it desires what is contrary to the will of God and His law, let us not indulge it, so that we may be Christians not merely in name, but in truth. Amen.
